blocks.text: WAREHOUSE CLEANOUT FAQ
Warehouse Cleanout Services in Toronto — FAQs

items.q: What does a warehouse cleanout in Toronto actually cost?
a: The racking and machinery drive most of it, plus what is on the floor and how the site lets us work. Access matters more here than in the suburbs — a building with one shared door and nowhere to stage adds real hours. We come and look, give you a number in writing, and that is the number.

items.q: We're clearing the building for demolition, not handing it back. Do your warehouse cleanout services cover that?
a: Yes, and it is most of our Toronto industrial work now. We sequence the clearance to your demolition contractor’s mobilisation date, take everything out in one programme, and issue documentation per building for the site record. No lease inspection to satisfy, but the contractor’s date does not move and we work backwards from it.

items.q: Our site has one shared dock and no yard. Is that a problem for a warehouse cleanout?
a: It is the normal situation on a Toronto industrial site and we plan for it rather than discovering it. Staging, truck movements and timing get worked out before dispatch, and where the street needs occupying we arrange that in advance. On a tight Junction or Riverdale site that planning is the difference between finishing and stalling.

items.q: The building has presses, compressors and an old crane. Can that come out in the warehouse cleanout?
a: Machinery and legacy plant are routine on older Toronto industrial — presses, benches, compressors, dust extraction, overhead cranes on standard installations. It comes out with everything else, with scrap steel weighed and recycled. If an installation needs an engineer’s sign-off we will tell you at the walkthrough rather than mid-job.

items.q: Do you provide warehouse cleanout services across North York and Scarborough?
a: Yes. Live Junk Free serves commercial and warehouse properties throughout Toronto, including North York, Scarborough, Etobicoke, East York, York and Downtown Toronto.
